assumptions: The generator decides the gemini-cli set. It emits 12 commands, one per skill with a skill.yaml, not the 6 the issue counted. The other 6 (judomaster, manhunter, mission-briefing, rewind, ship, shiva) were missing, which is the same drift, so they are added. That includes canary-ship, which the plugin keeps internal. agents/commands is not registered in the plugin manifest, so it ships nowhere new.

The generator is the CLI CI already uses: @harness-engineering/cli@12, resolved through npx. 12.10.1 locally, and 12.7.0 also produced byte-identical output. A future @12 minor that changes the template will red the gate with no repo change. Every gate message names the generator version for that reason.

The regeneration only changed inlined SKILL.md text. To check this, each file's SKILL.md at its last-touch commit was regenerated with the current CLI: 4 of 6 were byte-identical, and the remaining 2 differed only inside the SKILL.md section, never the template.
Only the gemini-cli half is in scope. The claude-code commands have their own drift: 5 missing, and mission-briefing hand-edited. That is filed as a follow-up and not touched here.
The generator output holds no absolute or machine-specific paths. SKILL.md paths are repo-relative because it runs in a scratch tree shaped like the repo, so nothing needs normalising.

The real-repo test case needs the harness CLI on PATH, so it runs locally only (describe.runIf). CI enforcement is the blocking step in harness-quality.yml validate, which abstains (exit 3, step fails) when the generator is unavailable.
